ety.text: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish عارف (arif), from Arabic عَارِف (ʕārif, “knowing”), active participle of عَرَفَ (ʕarafa, “to know”).
Mediopassive form of active bashkoj (“to connect, unite”). From bashkë (“together, simultaneously”) + o (vowel stem) + -hem (“I”) (mediopassive 1st pers. sg. personal suffix).
From bir (“son”) + -s- + -oj.

From cule + -aq, also noticed as cylaq and currulaq.

From Proto-Albanian *spālai, from Proto-Indo-European *spel (“to cleave, break”). Related to fyell and fell. Compare Greek φωλιά (foliá, “nest”), from Ancient Greek φωλεά (phōleá).
From Proto-Albanian *ga-daina, deadjectival from Proto-Indo-European *dh₂ey-nos, from *deh₂y- (“to divide”) (Albanian daj). More at daj.

ety.text: From Ottoman Turkish شفقات (Şevket) from Arabic شَفَقَة (šafaqa, “compassion, solicitude”).
From Proto-Albanian *iš-gardā, etymologically connected with gardh (“fence”). Connected to Romanian zgardă.
Borrowed from Latin explico. Compare Italian spiegare.

Singular form of a more spread plural tirq, cognate to Romanian tureac (“top (of a boot)”), tureatcă. Either an old loanword from an East Germanic language, Gepid or Gothic *𐌸𐌹𐌿𐌷𐌱𐍂𐍉𐌺𐍃 (*þiuhbrōks) (cf. Old High German theobroch (“gaiters”), English thigh, breeches), via Late Latin tubrucus, or, a more probable theory, a derivative of tjerr.
From Proto-Albanian *trem(b)-, from Proto-Indo-European *trem- (“to tripp, patter, tremble”). Cognate to Latin tremo (“to tremble”). A formation with labial "epenthesis" in stem auslaut.
From ujë + var.
From vreshtar (“viticulturist, winegrower”) + -i.
A prefixed formation of shtirë; vë- + shtirë.
